name: United States v. Al Capone (federal income-tax prosecution, 1931–1932)
summary: Federal prosecution of Chicago crime boss Alphonse Capone for income-tax evasion. His conviction was affirmed by the Seventh Circuit in 1932 (Capone v. United States, 56 F.2d 927). He is widely associated with violent crime, but this federal case concerned tax offenses.

knownPrimarySources.title: Capone v. United States, 56 F.2d 927 (7th Cir. 1932)
Capone v. Aderhold, 2 F. Supp. 280 (N.D. Ga. 1933)
Guzik v. United States, 54 F.2d 618 (7th Cir. 1931) — associate's tax case

rationale: Strong hook with a crisp, single federal legal outcome. It is the ideal test of the allegation-vs-conviction rule: much of the violence attributed to Capone was never adjudicated, so the script must keep it attributed while stating the tax conviction plainly.
risks: Heavy folklore and myth online (Untouchables lore) — many claims will be CONTRADICTED or DISCOVERY_ONLY
Violence claims are mostly allegation; guilt labels must be avoided for unadjudicated acts
